title: Podium — Provider Quality
description: Podium's probe verdicts, ranked by provider. Reads /api/metrics; see docs/configuration.md#metrics.

panels.title: Managed channels
panels.description: Channels podium stewards — the population the whole dashboard describes. Unmanaged channels are never probed, so their providers' quality is invisible here by design.

panels.title: Healthy primaries
panels.description: Share of channels whose slot-0 stream podium would rank as usable — alive, not a black screen, not starved. This is the number a viewer experiences.

panels.title: Alive (of probed)
panels.description: Share of assigned streams that answered the probe at all, excluding never-probed ones. Dead, black and starved all count against it.

panels.title: Black screens
panels.description: Alive streams whose sampled window was mostly black — the 'channel unavailable' slate every quality metric misses. Any nonzero count deserves a look.

panels.title: Awaiting first probe
panels.description: Assigned streams with no verdict yet. Nonzero while a provider is newly added and being worked through; stuck nonzero means the prober is not keeping up.

panels.title: Catalogue age
panels.description: Since a pass last wrote the full channel/stream snapshot. Past twice the freshness target (PODIUM_MAX_AGE_MS, 24h by default) the ordering itself is stale. The orange threshold assumes the default.

panels.title: The providers, side by side
panels.description: Everything podium has measured, one row per provider. SCOPE: assigned streams on managed channels only — a provider's unassigned catalogue (tens of thousands of streams) is never probed, by design; a provider can only be judged on the streams actually given to channels. 'Starved' = alive but under podium's bitrate floor; %FHD+ counts UHD+FHD of probed streams (dead ones count against it). 'Score' is the median of the same 0..1 score the ranker uses, over usable streams only. 'Win rate' = primaries divided by the channels the provider appears on at any slot — how often it wins a contest it is actually in. 'Primaries' is channels whose slot-0 source is that provider. READ THE LAST TWO COLUMNS FIRST: '% meas.' is the share of streams that answered whose bitrate was really measured rather than taken from the container's own claim — a low value means 'Median kbps' and 'Score' rest on very little. 'Verdict age' is the median age of the verdicts this whole row is computed from; a lane pinned at its provider's max_streams gets probed least often, so the provider you most want to judge carries the stalest numbers. Green is inside PODIUM_MAX_AGE_MS (24h by default).

panels.title: Primaries by provider
panels.description: Channels whose slot-0 source each provider holds right now — the headline number while reassigning channels to new providers.

panels.title: Primaries over time
panels.description: The same counts as history: every step is a reorder writing a different provider into slot 0. Watch the new providers' lines climb as channels get reassigned to them.

panels.title: Median measured bitrate (kbps)
panels.description: Median across each provider's assigned streams, MEASURED bitrates only — a declared bitrate is exactly the number this exists not to trust. Providers with nothing measured yet show no bar. Per-resolution medians exist on the same family (resolution label) for comparing like against like — 4500 kbps is generous at 720p and thin at 1080p.

panels.title: Verdict states by provider
panels.description: Every assigned stream, stacked by what the probe found. One-hot in podium's ranking precedence: a black stream counts only as black, a starved one only as starved. 'Unprobed' is streams still awaiting their first verdict.

panels.title: Resolution mix by provider
panels.description: What the streams actually deliver, from ffprobe's measured height — not the '[1080p]' in their names. Unknown = dead, unprobed, or no dimensions; it is the share of a provider's assignment you cannot count on.

panels.title: Median measured bitrate by resolution
panels.description: The same medians as the scorecard, split by what the stream actually is. A single median across a mixed line-up scores a provider partly on its channel mix: 4500 kbps is generous at 720p and thin at 1080p, so a provider carrying more SD and HD looks worse than it is. Compare down a column, not across. Blank means nothing measured in that bucket — not zero. Streams whose height never resolved are left out; they are in the scorecard's 'all' median.

panels.title: Why streams die, by provider
panels.description: The dead counts above, bucketed by ffmpeg's last words. auth = credentials or ban; not_found = the stream does not exist any more; client_error = refused for another 4xx reason, such as a rate limit or connection cap; server_error = the provider's side falling over; unreachable = network path/DNS; unsupported = a format ffmpeg cannot demux; probe_error is PODIUM's own failure (missing ffprobe, unparseable payload) and must not be held against the provider. The buckets partition each provider's dead count exactly.

panels.title: Every managed channel, its sources in Dispatcharr order
panels.description: Slot 0 is what plays first; each row below it is a fallback in the order podium wrote. State is podium's verdict for that exact stream — check a provider's name against its slots to see who is carrying whom. Needs PODIUM_METRICS_CHANNELS on (default). THE JOIN IS IN THE PROMQL, not a transformation: Grafana's join-by-field takes one field and cannot key on (channel_id, slot), so every query folds info and state onto its own series and all three carry identical labels, which the merge transformation lines up row by row. max by also drops pod, so a restart overlap cannot split a row.

panels.title: Worker
panels.description: Whether a worker holds the SQLite lock with a fresh heartbeat. The heartbeat rides idle sleeps, so STOPPED means the loop is gone, not resting.

panels.title: Run phase
panels.description: Where the current pass is: fetching, planning, probing, paused, done or failed.

panels.title: Oldest verdict vs target
panels.description: Age of the least recently probed managed stream, as a share of the freshness target (PODIUM_MAX_AGE_MS). Over 100% is routine when a provider allows few connections, because its probes get deferred. Holding above 200% means the pacer has stopped keeping up.

panels.title: Deferred this run
panels.description: Streams the current pass wanted to probe but could not, because their provider had no spare connection. A provider capped at one connection defers whenever it is in use. This is the main reason verdicts age past the target.

panels.title: Failed runs (24h)
panels.description: Passes that ended in an error. A handful a week is normal. Several in an hour is not, and the worker heartbeat stays green through it.

panels.title: Probes skipped (24h)
panels.description: Probes abandoned when a pass aborted.

panels.title: Verdict freshness
panels.description: The least recently probed managed stream against the freshness target. A sawtooth is the pacer catching up. A line that climbs through the dashed 2x mark and stays there means the pacer has stopped keeping up.

panels.title: Probing per hour
panels.description: Streams probed, probes skipped by an aborted pass, dead verdicts recorded, and passes that failed. Failed runs are drawn on the right axis.

panels.title: Lineup changes per hour
panels.description: What podium writes back to Dispatcharr: channels reordered, streams added to channels (PODIUM_AUTO_ASSIGN) and dead streams removed (PODIUM_REMOVE_DEAD_AFTER_CHECKS). A reorder spike after a quiet stretch usually follows a provider coming back or falling over.

panels.title: Probe lanes by provider
panels.description: Per-provider concurrency in the current pass: streams queued, streams being probed now, and the lane limit (dashed). A lane whose queue stays up while in-flight sits at its limit is the provider holding the pass back. Only providers in the current pass report a lane.

panels.title: Pass size and deferral
panels.description: Streams each pass selected and probed, against the streams it had to defer for lack of provider capacity. Deferred work is what pushes the oldest verdict past the target.
